Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of dry heaving and stifling a sneeze in a young male is classic for the Macklin effect, where increased alveolar pressure causes rupture and air tracks along bronchovascular sheaths into the mediastinum (spontaneous pneumomediastinum). The chest X-ray findings of linear lucencies along the hilar/paratracheal regions and subcutaneous emphysema without pleural effusion or hydropneumothorax support this benign etiology over esophageal perforation.
